canonicalExplanation.summary: `class Circle extends Shape` says **every Circle is a Shape** and can be used anywhere a Shape is expected. That promise only holds if the subclass honours the superclass's **whole contract**: it can't reject operations the base supports or break its rules. The subclass must initialise the superclass part first, calling **`super(...)`** as the first statement of its constructor (Java inserts `super()` automatically if you don't, which fails if Shape has no no-arg constructor). Keep superclass fields **private** and expose only deliberate `protected` or public methods, so subclasses can't corrupt shared state. If a subclass would need to throw "unsupported" for base operations, inheritance is the wrong tool.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner makes `ReadOnlyList extends ArrayList` and overrides add() to throw. Code that adds to any ArrayList crashes when given one. They also forget super(...) in Circle, and the compile fails because Shape has no no-arg constructor. Circle extends Shape because every Circle supports the complete Shape area contract and initializes required Shape state through super(...). In this lesson you'll evaluate and implement a small inheritance hierarchy without exposing mutable representation.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Constructors and invariants** (validation and this(...)) and **Interfaces** (depending on contracts).

sections.heading: The rule: subtypes honour the whole base contract
When not to inherit

includes: Decide whether a subtype can honour the full base contract before using extends.
Initialise superclasses with super(...) and keep superclass state private.
excludes: Multiple inheritance of state (not possible in Java).

outcomes: Evaluate and implement a small inheritance hierarchy without exposing mutable representation.

examples.title: Circle extends Shape, honestly
examples.situation: Circle extends Shape because every Circle supports the complete Shape area contract and initializes required Shape state through super(...).
walkthrough: **Every Circle supports the complete Shape area contract:** area() returns a non-negative value for any valid radius.
**Initializes required Shape state through super(...):** super("circle") runs first and validates the name.
**Private representation:** name stays private in Shape, and describe(new Circle(2)) will print circle 12.57.
examples.result: Code written for Shape works with Circle and no special cases.

examples.title: The read-only list
examples.situation: ReadOnlyList extends ArrayList and throws UnsupportedOperationException from add.
walkthrough: Code expecting any ArrayList assumes add works.
The subclass rejects a base operation, so it isn't substitutable.
Use List.copyOf or Collections.unmodifiableList, which are designed as read-only views.
examples.result: No ArrayList-using code is surprised by an exception.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Inheritance is appropriate whenever two classes share fields or helper code, even if the subtype rejects base operations.
misconceptions.correction: extends promises full substitutability. Sharing code without honouring the whole contract calls for composition or a shared helper instead.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The read-only list", which base operation was rejected?

analogy.example: Inheritance is like **a franchise**: a Circle restaurant under the Shape brand must serve **everything on the brand's menu**, to the same standard. A franchise that refuses half the menu isn't really part of the brand. And the head office's recipes (private fields) stay in the head office.
usefulFor: super(...) = opening under the brand first
limitations: Franchises can add dishes; subclasses can add methods.
Refusing menu items breaks every customer's expectations.

steps.explanation: Circle initializes required Shape state through super(...) first.
The subclass validates its own state after the base part.
Every Circle supports the complete Shape area contract, so describe needs no special case.

nearTransfer.prompt: Add a Rectangle extends Shape with validated width and height. Write one test method taking Shape and run it on a Circle and a Rectangle.

farTransfer.prompt: Evaluate three proposed hierarchies (Square extends Rectangle with independent setters, Manager extends Employee, Stack extends ArrayList). For each, decide inherit or compose, justify with the base contract, and implement one correctly.
scaffold: Test the base contract against the subtype.
Look for rejected or surprising operations.

remediation.explanation: Before writing extends, run the **base class's tests against the subclass** in your head: does every one still pass? If not, compose instead.

recap.summary: To implement a sound inheritance hierarchy, extend only when every subclass can honour the complete base contract, initialise the superclass first with super(...), keep superclass fields private behind deliberate methods, and switch to composition when a subtype would reject or change base behaviour.
